title: Migrate address_collision.json corpus + test_address_collision_vectors.py to upstream AddrForKey
description: Discovered during i72x.6 (worker3). test/vectors/address_collision.json embeds rejected native-profile bound addresses (e.g. 020e:02a5:0225:b4ba:0c02:a502:25b4:baaa for RFC8032 key d75a98...) and python/tests/test_address_collision_vectors.py has matching hardcoded expectations (line 156-157). 3 tests fail pre-existing: bound_native_same_key_is_idempotent_and_expires, bound_native_rejects_mismatch_and_invalid_identity_inputs_atomically, test_public_binding_helper_returns_canonical_address. Migration subtleties: (1) verify_native_address_binding (python/src/lichen/address_collision.py) now binds to upstream AddrForKey, so bound addresses must rebind to upstream; (2) NEGATIVE vectors must stay negative — the '20e:2a5...' idempotent-variant and '030e:...' subnet-form entries rely on specific invalidity (missing 0x02 prefix / subnet bit) that naive rebind breaks; (3) scenario logic (collision sets keyed by address) must be re-verified op-by-op after rebinding, not mass-rewritten. Attempted mass-rebind (23 addrs) regressed 3->8 failures; reverted. Recommend: rebind only observe_bound_native positive ops to AddrForKey(pk), re-derive each negative's invalid form from the NEW upstream address (e.g. idempotent-variant = upstream with 0x02 prefix stripped to '20e...' form, subnet-form = upstream with byte0|0x01), then update test hardcodes to the new upstream bytes. Oracle: production yggdrasil_address (7pt2, byte-equal to upstream Go).
